newsitem.title: FRANCE: KLM weighs airlift to beat French truck ba.
newsitem.headline: KLM weighs airlift to beat French truck ba.

text.p: KLM Cargo said it was considering starting a weekend freighter service between Italy and Schiphol because of a French government ban on weekend road haulage traffic to be introduced from March 24.
Earlier this month, KLM Cargo started a week-end freighter service from Zaragoza to Amsterdam, using a 30 tonne-capacity Belfast aircraft, in anticipation of the ban.

"Italy is a very important market for us and we have very dense trucking operation over weekend periods carrying airfreight to Amsterdam to catch both freighter and passenger flights," KLM Cargo's Paris-based Operations manager, Southern Europe, Simon Groenenboom, told Reuters.

Currently, truckers are allowed to return back to their home location. But after the ban comes into force vehicles, weighing more than 7.5 tonnes, will be banned from French roads between 2200 local (2100 gmt) Saturday until the same time on Sunday.

"While discussions and lobbying is going on between government ministers and road haulage associations and the European commission, we are not too optimistic that the French authorities will withdraw the ban," Groenenboom said.
KLM Cargo was considering a number of contingency options to cope with the ban.

"We could bring forward cut-off times at our pallet consolidation centre at Milan to allow trucks to leave earlier for Amsterdam so as to avoid transiting France when the ban is in place. Other possibilities would be to modify itineraries or use rail transport. However, it's very likely we will need to resort to an air cargo operation of some kind out of Italy, probably using a wide-bodied aircraft, which could carry up to 60 tonnes or more but clearly this would depend on availability."

"Another question would be where in Italy, would planes for Amsterdam fly from. The obvious choice would be Milan but with about 50 percent of our Italian freight originating in the south of the country - notably Rome, Bologna and Florence, a gateway in this region can't be excluded," he added.

If this was the case, cut-off times for freight in the Milan region could be brought forward to allow earlier trucking despatch with an air cargo operation thus being limited to freight from southern Italy, Groenenboom said.
"However, for the moment we are leaving our all options open will probably make a decision in the next two to three weeks," Groenenboom stated.
